name: Mykonos
tagline: Cycladic glamour, windmills and the Aegean's liveliest shores.
bestMonths: May, Jun, Jul, Aug and Sep
whenBlurb: This is a scene, not a calendar: come late May to September when the beach clubs and dinners run at full tilt, peaking July-August; the island all but closes in winter.

ourTake.lede: Mykonos is two islands at once: the polished beach-club and party circuit, and a quieter Cycladic island of white lanes, windmills and little churches that most visitors barely see. Decide which one you came for. If it's the scene, base near town and book the beach clubs ahead; if it's the calm, take a boat to Delos, eat at the far tavernas, and treat the crowds in Little Venice as a sunset ritual to visit once, not live in.
ourTake.comeIf: You want polished Cycladic glamour, beach clubs and a yacht day, with dinners that run late.
ourTake.skipIf: You are travelling with young children or want quiet, unspoilt island life away from the scene.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Cali Mykonos
credentials: MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
WELL Certified, Gold (health & wellbeing building standard)
Condé Nast Traveller, featured; 'one of the most luxurious hotels in the Cyclades'
items.description: The island's most talked-about newer address, a serene stone-and-marble retreat on Mykonos's calmer side, built for privacy rather than the party.

items.name: Belvedere Mykonos
items.area: Chora (School of Fine Arts district, above town)
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
Home to Matsuhisa Mykonos (Nobu Matsuhisa) and Six Senses Spa
items.description: The cosmopolitan heart of Mykonos glamour, a sun-bleached Cycladic labyrinth walking distance from town, home to the island's landmark Matsuhisa restaurant and a Six Senses spa.

items.name: Santa Marina, a Luxury Collection Resort
credentials: The Luxury Collection (Marriott)
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
Home to Mykonos Social by Jason Atherton and Buddha-Bar Beach
items.description: A full private-peninsula resort on Ornos Bay with its own curve of sand, Marriott's Luxury Collection flagship on the island, and home to Jason Atherton's Mykonos Social.

items.name: Katikies Mykonos
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
items.description: An adults-only cliffside hideaway above Agios Ioannis beach, facing the island's best sunsets, all-white, serene, and almost every suite with its own plunge pool or jetted tub.

items.name: Kalesma Mykonos
credentials: MICHELIN One Key (2025), inaugural Greece selection
Home to Pere Ubu fine dining
items.description: A hilltop village of Cycladic suites and villas overlooking the Aegean, nothing smaller than a one-bedroom suite, each with its own heated infinity pool. One of Greece's first MICHELIN Key hotels.

items.name: Bill&Coo Mykonos
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
items.description: An intimate, adults-only design hotel on the water at Megali Ammos, a short walk from town, polished, romantic, and known for one of the island's more serious kitchens.

items.name: Cavo Tagoo Mykonos
credentials: Design Hotels member
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
Home to Kiku (Japanese)
items.description: The island's original design landmark, carved white into the cliff above the sea just north of Chora, with a saltwater infinity pool and Kiku, its long-running Japanese restaurant.

items.name: Mykonos Blu, a Grecotel Resort
credentials: Grecotel, Exclusive Resort
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
items.description: A Cycladic resort strung above glamorous Psarou beach, bungalows and villas cascading to the sand, steps from the island's most famous beach-club stretch.

items.name: Kensho Ornos
credentials: MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
BIG SEE Design Award, architecture & interiors
items.description: A boutique house of understated, natural-material luxury above Ornos Bay, small, design-forward and calm, with a rooftop restaurant over the water.

items.name: Mykonos Town (Chora)
items.description: The whitewashed labyrinth of Mykonos, bougainvillea-draped lanes deliberately built to confuse pirates, now lined with boutiques, cafes and blue-shuttered doorways at every turn. Wander with no map; late afternoon light and early morning (before the cruise crowds) are the honeymoon-photo hours.

items.name: Little Venice (Alefkandra)
items.description: A row of 18th-century sea-captains' houses with wooden balconies leaning straight over the Aegean, so the waves lap at the walls. The most romantic sundowner in Mykonos, book a waterfront table and let the sky change colour with a glass in hand.

items.name: The Windmills of Kato Mili
items.description: Five white 16th-century windmills on the hill above Little Venice, the single most iconic image of Mykonos, catching the meltemi winds that once ground the island's grain. Time it for sunset when the whole ridge glows gold.

items.name: Panagia Paraportiani Church
items.description: A sculptural white cluster of five chapels melted into one form, begun in the 15th century, one of the most photographed churches in all Greece. Pure Cycladic minimalism; catch it against a blue sky or the last pink of dusk.

items.name: Aegean Maritime Museum
items.description: A quiet, beautifully-kept museum of Greek seafaring in a traditional Chora mansion, with model ships, old maps and a leafy garden holding the restored 19th-century lantern of the Armenistis lighthouse. A cool, cultured half-hour away from the sun and the crowds.

items.name: Lena's House
items.description: A perfectly preserved 19th-century middle-class Mykonian home, furniture, embroidery, framed photographs and all, kept exactly as it was lived in. A small, intimate window into island life before the glamour, right beside the Maritime Museum.

items.name: Matoyianni Street
items.description: The main artery of Chora and the island's luxury shopping spine, Louis Vuitton, Dior and Greek designers between the whitewashed walls, alive until well past midnight. The place to see and be seen while browsing.

items.name: Rarity Gallery
items.description: Greece's leading contemporary art gallery since 1994, on Kalogera Street, showing international names and hyperrealist sculpture that stops passers-by in their tracks. A serious, collectable stop for art-minded travellers between beach and dinner.

items.name: Dio Horia Gallery
items.description: A three-floor contemporary art platform in a converted Mykonian house, with an atmospheric rooftop bar looking over the town's rooftops. Cutting-edge exhibitions and a cocktail with a view, in one address.

items.name: Panagia Tourliani Monastery
items.description: The island's most important monastery, founded in 1542 in the inland village of Ano Mera, with a spectacular gilded Baroque altarpiece carved by Florentine artists in 1775. A serene, devotional counterpoint to the coast, and a genuine glimpse of local faith.

items.name: Ano Mera Village
items.description: The one real inland village on Mykonos, a tree-shaded square with tavernas serving unhurried, authentic island cooking, far from the port glamour. Where families and multi-gen groups go for a slow, honest Greek lunch.

items.name: Armenistis Lighthouse
items.description: An 1891 stone lighthouse on the island's north-western tip, built after a shipwreck, looking across the strait to Tinos. One of the least-crowded, most cinematic sunset perches on Mykonos, pack a picnic and arrive early.

items.name: 180° Sunset Bar
items.description: Perched on the walls of the old Castle Panigirakis at the highest point above town, this bar delivers the full panoramic sweep over Chora, the windmills and the sea as the sun drops. A polished spot for a celebratory sundown cocktail.

items.name: Caprice Bar, Little Venice
items.description: The classic waterfront sunset bar of Little Venice, where the Aegean laps at the terrace and the whole crowd turns to watch the sky. Get there before sunset to claim a table right at the water's edge.

items.name: Psarou Beach
items.description: The glamour beach of Mykonos, a sheltered golden crescent of turquoise water fronted by Nammos, where yachts anchor offshore and the jet-set sunbathe. Chic, family-friendly and firmly see-and-be-seen; book a lounger well ahead in season.

items.name: Ornos Beach
items.description: The most family-friendly beach on the island, a calm, shallow south-coast bay with good hotels, restaurants and water taxis at its doorstep. Easygoing and central, ideal for multi-generation trips with young children.

items.name: Platis Gialos Beach
items.description: The best all-round beach on Mykonos, a long stretch of golden sand, clear water and a good range of tavernas and beach bars, plus the hub for the south-coast water taxi that hops between every beach. Wonderfully practical for a full, easy beach day.

items.name: Paradise Beach
items.description: The legendary party beach, golden sand by day that turns into open-air dance floors as the sun sets, home to the famous Cavo Paradiso club on the cliff above. Framed here as the scene: go for the spectacle, or skip it if you want quiet.

items.name: Super Paradise Beach
items.description: The other half of the party legend, a stunning cove with brilliant water, beach clubs and daytime dancing that runs late into the afternoon. Iconic, hedonistic and inclusive; best appreciated by those who want the full Mykonos energy.

items.name: Elia Beach
items.description: The longest and most sophisticated of the organised south-coast beaches, broad, sandy, with space to breathe, good clubs and watersports at one end. A smart choice for a relaxed but well-serviced beach day.

items.name: Kalo Livadi Beach
items.description: Golden sand and clear water without the south-coast party machine, longer than Psarou, less crowded than Platis Gialos, with excellent beachfront restaurants. The sweet spot for couples and families who want style without the crush.

items.name: Agios Sostis Beach
items.description: A completely undeveloped north-coast beach, no sunbeds, no bars, no buses, just raw Cycladic coastline reached on foot. For a day of true privacy, with Kiki's Tavern hidden on the hill above for lunch.

items.name: Fokos Beach
items.description: One of the last wild, unspoilt beaches on Mykonos, remote, wind-brushed and gloriously empty, with a single well-loved taverna at the back. The island's answer to those who've had enough of the scene and want silence.

items.name: Panormos Beach
items.description: A long, handsome north-coast bay that mixes an undeveloped stretch with the stylish Principote beach club at one end. Fewer crowds than the south coast, with an effortless bohemian-chic mood by day.

items.name: Nammos Beach Club
items.description: The most famous beach club in the Mediterranean, on Psarou sand, a legendary scene of magnums, designer boutiques and celebrity-watching, with genuinely excellent seafood. The apex of Mykonos see-and-be-seen; reserve weeks ahead in high summer.

items.name: Scorpios
items.description: The island's most-referenced beach club, on a headland at Paraga, less about wild partying and more about a curated 'music, movement and community' ritual that builds into a sunset ceremony. Bohemian-luxe and unforgettable; book day beds far ahead.

items.name: Principote
items.description: The chic beach club on Panormos, striking a balance between glamour and relaxed comfort away from the south-coast intensity. Stylish loungers, good food and a calmer, more elegant scene, a fine choice for couples.

items.name: Delos Archaeological Site
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Delos
items.description: The sacred birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, a uninhabited island 30 minutes by boat, an entire Greco-Roman city frozen in stone, from the Terrace of the Lions to the mosaic-floored House of Dionysos. The essential half-day of Mykonos; hire a private guide and go early before the heat.

items.name: Archaeological Museum of Delos
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Delos
items.description: The on-site museum housing the finest sculpture and mosaics recovered from Delos, including the original Naxian lions moved indoors for protection. A cool, essential stop that brings the ruins outside back to life.

items.name: Private Catamaran Day Cruise
items.description: The definitive Mykonos indulgence, a full day on a private catamaran or motor yacht, sailing past Delos to swim in the aquamarine coves of Rhenia, with a chef, a crew and no one else aboard. Perfect for a honeymoon, a milestone or a family day at sea; veg and dietary menus arranged on request.

items.name: Rhenia Island
items.description: The uninhabited sister-island beside Delos, ringed with empty white-sand coves and impossibly clear water, reachable only by boat. The reward at the heart of a private cruise: swimming and snorkelling in near-total solitude.

items.name: Watersports & Diving
items.description: The organised south-coast beaches, Platis Gialos, Elia, Paradise, offer everything from jet-skis and paddleboards to scuba diving over clear reefs. Easy, well-run fun for active families and teenagers between the sunbathing.

items.name: Kiki's Tavern, Agios Sostis
items.description: A cult taverna above quiet Agios Sostis with no electricity, no phone and no reservations, everything grilled over charcoal, the salads famous, the queue part of the ritual. A gloriously unpretentious island lunch that money genuinely can't fast-track.

items.name: Kounelas Fish Tavern
items.description: A long-standing family fish taverna in the back lanes of Chora, where the day's catch is chosen at the counter and the louza and grilled seafood are the real thing. The kind of honest, atmospheric table locals still keep for themselves.

items.name: M-eating Restaurant
items.description: A refined Chora restaurant championing Greek produce done with modern polish, a strong place to taste island specialities like kopanisti cheese in an elegant setting. Intimate and well-suited to a quieter celebration dinner.

items.name: Interni Restaurant
items.description: A design-led courtyard restaurant in the old town, mixing Mediterranean and Asian technique with Greek produce, that turns into a buzzing scene as the night goes on. Dinner and glamour in one; the tuna tartare and lobster are the signatures.

items.name: Bill & Coo Fine Dining
credentials: Relais & Chateaux hotel dining
items.description: The acclaimed dining rooms of the Relais & Chateaux Bill & Coo hotel, from the refined YEVO tasting menu to Beefbar on the coast, some of the most polished cooking on the island. A destination dinner for a special occasion, overlooking the bay.

items.name: Local Flavours, Kopanisti & Louza
items.description: Two things to eat before you leave: kopanisti, the peppery, tangy Mykonian cheese spread on rusk, and louza, the island's cinnamon-and-pepper cured pork, Mykonos's answer to prosciutto. Ask any good taverna, they are the true taste of the island beneath the glamour.

items.name: Cavo Paradiso
items.description: The clifftop superclub above Paradise Beach that brings the world's top DJs to Mykonos every summer, dancing under the stars until dawn. The pinnacle of the island's legendary nightlife, framed here as the scene for those who want it.

items.name: Fokos & the Wild North Tavernas
items.description: The rugged, taverna-dotted north coast, Fokos, Ftelia, Agios Sostis, where a rough drive rewards you with empty beaches and slow, sea-facing lunches. The antidote to the port: this is where Mykonos still feels like a real Cycladic island.

items.name: Day Trip to Tinos
items.description: The neighbouring island 20-30 minutes by ferry, its famous pilgrimage church, marble-carving villages, wild artichokes and its own louza make it the best-value escape in the Cyclades. A quiet, devotional, deeply Greek counterpoint to Mykonos's shine.

items.name: Matsuhisa Mykonos
credentials: Nobu Matsuhisa (global restaurant group)
At Belvedere Mykonos, The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Nobu Matsuhisa's Mykonos table at the Belvedere, the island's landmark restaurant for two decades, and the world's original poolside Matsuhisa, serving the signature black cod miso and new-style sashimi.

items.name: Mykonos Social by Jason Atherton
credentials: Jason Atherton (MICHELIN-starred chef, London, Social group)
At Santa Marina, a Luxury Collection Resort
items.description: British chef Jason Atherton's Mediterranean table above Ornos Bay, inventive small plates and grilled seafood on a terrace made for long sunset dinners.

items.name: Pere Ubu at Kalesma
credentials: At Kalesma Mykonos, MICHELIN One Key (2025)
items.description: The hilltop dining room at Kalesma, refined Cycladic-Mediterranean cooking with produce-led menus, on a terrace with one of the island's finest Aegean panoramas.

items.name: Interni Restaurant
credentials: Long-running Chora landmark (est. 2000), the original dinner-to-party destination in Mykonos Town
items.description: A secret-garden institution in the heart of Chora since 2000, refined Mediterranean cooking, serious cocktails and the island's original dinner-into-party evening.

items.name: Kiku at Cavo Tagoo
credentials: At Cavo Tagoo Mykonos, Design Hotels member
items.description: The long-established Japanese kitchen at Cavo Tagoo, sushi, sashimi and modern rolls served against the hotel's cliffside cave-pool setting.

items.name: Beefbar Mykonos
credentials: Beefbar (international restaurant group, founded Monte-Carlo)
At Bill&Coo The Coast, Agios Ioannis bay
items.description: The Mykonos outpost of the international Beefbar group, premium cuts and world grills on a beachfront terrace at Agios Ioannis, run by the Giraudi family.

items.name: M-eating
credentials: Greek Gastronomy Guide, featured
Long-established Chora fine-dining landmark
items.description: Chef Panagiotis Menardos's contemporary take on Cycladic and Greek recipes, in a restored early-1900s townhouse in the heart of town, the island's most respected Greek fine-dining room.

items.name: Bakalo
credentials: Established Chora favourite (est. 2010); expanded internationally (Miami Beach outpost)
items.description: A warm, unpretentious Greek eatery in the Lakka quarter of old town, honest regional recipes done well, long a favourite of visiting names for its lack of fuss.

items.name: Kastro's
credentials: Little Venice landmark since 1976, among the island's most established and photographed tables
items.description: On the water's edge in 18th-century Little Venice since 1976, one of the most photographed rooms on the island, its balcony tables set between old stone walls and the splashing Aegean.

items.name: Kadena
credentials: Established waterfront restaurant on Gialos, Mykonos Town
items.description: An all-day room on the Gialos waterfront in town, Mediterranean cooking of pasta, seafood and grills with the harbour and fishing boats in view.

items.name: Alemagou
credentials: Star Wine List, recognised wine programme
Long-running Ftelia beach institution
items.description: A bohemian beach taverna on windswept Ftelia, Aegean-fusion cooking, a serious wine list and a laid-back, barefoot afternoon-into-evening mood far from the glossy clubs.

items.name: Scorpios
credentials: Operated by Soho House / Soho Roc House, the island's defining beach-club-to-party institution
items.description: The island's most influential day-to-night beach club, a Soho House-run temple of long lunches, ritual sunsets and world-class DJs on the rocks above Paraga, part beach club, part cultural marketplace.

items.name: Nammos
credentials: Internationally renowned Psarou beach club, the island's most famous; a global luxury-lifestyle brand
items.description: The global byword for Mykonos beach glamour, a Psarou institution since 2003 that grew from a beach taverna into one of the most famous, and most expensive, beach clubs in the world.

items.name: Principote
credentials: Renowned Panormos beach club, among the most prestigious in the Cyclades
items.description: A bohemian-luxe beach club on quieter Panormos, hand-crafted design, Mediterranean cooking and DJ-led afternoons that build into celebratory sunset parties.

items.name: SantAnna Mykonos
credentials: The largest beach club on Mykonos; home to Europe's largest saltwater pool
items.description: The island's largest beach club, built around the biggest saltwater pool in Europe, an amphitheatre of daybeds, restaurants and stage shows on Paraga.

items.name: Bar at Cavo Tagoo
credentials: At Cavo Tagoo Mykonos, Design Hotels member
items.description: The cliffside pool bar of the island's original design hotel, cocktails beside the cave-cut saltwater pool as the sun drops behind the Aegean.

items.name: Cavo Paradiso
credentials: DJ Mag Top 100 Clubs, ranked worldwide (2024, 2025, 2026)
items.description: Mykonos's legendary open-air superclub, a clifftop dancefloor above the Aegean that has hosted the world's biggest electronic names since 1993, and the island's one internationally ranked club.

items.name: Bonbonniere
credentials: Sister club to Bonbonniere London, a leading Mykonos Town nightclub
items.description: The glossy town nightclub of the Mykonos jet set, sister to London's Bonbonniere, a small, high-energy room known for star DJs, celebrity nights and theatrical champagne service.

items.name: VOID Mykonos
credentials: One of the largest nightclubs in Mykonos Town, a leading house/techno venue
items.description: A three-level house-and-techno club in town, one of the island's largest indoor clubs, with a music-first programme that draws a serious dance crowd.

plan.heading: 3 days in Mykonos, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The old town lanes at first light, Little Venice and the windmills before the day fills.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A slow lunch and the water at Scorpios or the calmer Kalo Livadi end of the island.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at the Belvedere's Nobu terrace or the tables of Bill & Coo above the bay.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private boat to Delos, the sacred island of Apollo, with a guide among the ruins.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: On to a quiet cove for the afternoon, the caïque anchored for swimming and lunch aboard.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Greek seafood at Kiki's-style simplicity, then a late table at Spilia carved into the rock.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A late start, then the fine sand and clear water of Agios Sostis or Fokos, away from the clubs.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at Alemagou on Ftelia, feet in the sand, then the drive back over the hills.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sunset drinks at 180° Sunset Bar by the old castle, then dinner at M-eating in town.

items.name: Chora (Mykonos Town)
items.description: The whitewashed maze of shops, bars and nightlife; suits those who want to walk everywhere and be in the thick of it.

items.name: Psarou / Platis Gialos
items.description: The polished south-coast beach strip with the marquee clubs and calm swimming; suits sun-and-scene travellers.

items.name: Ano Mera
items.description: The quiet inland village around its monastery, away from the crowds; suits those wanting local calm and space.

events.name: XLSIOR Festival
events.note: One of the world's largest LGBTQ+ dance festivals, taking over the island's clubs and beach venues for five to six days.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in the old town or Agios Lazaros for calm, away from the party beaches; the best clubs and beach restaurants require a reservation and a deposit in high summer, so arrange these before you land.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Mykonos (JMK), fifteen minutes from town, or arrive by private yacht; a chauffeur meets the flight and drives you to the villa or hotel.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car and driver for the beaches and coast; the old town is pedestrian-only, a deliberate maze best explored on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Networks are strong and an eSIM activates on arrival; wifi is standard, though beach clubs can be patchy at peak hours.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The euro; cards are taken everywhere, cash is handy at the smaller beach tavernas, and tipping around ten percent is welcomed at the busier venues.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: June and September are the sweet spot, warm, swimmable, sociable without August saturation; July-August is peak crowd and price, and the summer meltemi wind can whip the beaches and disrupt ferries.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Via Athens, no India nonstop. Fly Athens (IndiGo direct, or Gulf/Turkish carrier in business), then a 40-minute Aegean/Sky Express flight to Mykonos (JMK) or a high-speed ferry from Rafina. Direct seasonal European flights to Mykonos exist but connections are simpler through Athens; secure summer legs well ahead.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required; tap water is desalinated and brackish, use bottled. Safe and relaxed; main cautions are scooter/quad-bike risk and slippery Chora lanes at night. No altitude concern.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Fine for vegetarians, Greek meze, salads and grilled vegetables are everywhere, though Jain needs explicit instruction. Indian dining is limited; a private chef suits a longer stay, and Nice n Easy or Bill & Coo handle refined vegetarian requests well.
